title: U.S. stock futures steady after Nasdaq slides on OpenAI revenue concerns
full_text:
Nasdaq ends over 1% lower as tech stocks take a hit on OpenAI revenue report
Investing.com-- U.S. stock futures were little changed Thursday night after Wall Street fell for a second straight session, as concerns over OpenAI's revenue outlook weighed on artificial intelligence-related stocks and rising oil prices revived inflation worries.
S&P 500 Futures inched 0.1% higher to 7,825.25.0 points, while Nasdaq 100 Futures traded flat at 30,978.75 points by 20:26 ET (00:26 GMT). Dow Jones Futures traded 0.2% higher at 51,570.0 points.
In the regular session, the NASDAQ Composite fell 1.3% to 27,193.34, while the S&P 500 lost 0.5% to 7,765.36. The Dow Jones Industrial Average edged up 0.1% to 51,231.64, outperforming the broader market as technology shares came under pressure.
The pullback came two days after the Nasdaq Composite and S&P 500 reached record closing highs, with investors also assessing the outlook for interest rates ahead of the start of the third-quarter earnings season.
The technology-heavy Nasdaq bore the brunt of the selloff after a Financial Times report said OpenAI had told investors its annualized revenue was approaching $50 billion at the end of September, below the $70 billion figure previously reported by media outlets.
The discrepancy stemmed from differences in how OpenAI and rival Anthropic account for sales through cloud partners, the FT reported. Anthropic includes revenue from partners such as Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud, while OpenAI excludes those sales from its calculation, according to the report.
The figures raised questions about the scale of AI demand and the financial returns on heavy investment in computing infrastructure.
Chipmakers and companies financing AI infrastructure were among the session's biggest losers. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 3.4%, while Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) dropped 2.9%, Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) slid 3.9%, and Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) lost 4.8%.
Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) declined 4.4%, and Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) shed 5.5%, amid concerns about the financing required to support large-scale AI infrastructure projects.
Investors were also monitoring oil prices amid heightened concerns about Middle East supply disruptions. U.S. crude futures settled 3.6% higher, while Brent crude rose 4.1% above $104 per barrel, adding to inflation concerns at a time when borrowing costs remain elevated.
Hurricane-related production cuts in the Gulf of Mexico further tightened supply expectations.
Treasury yields retreated from their session highs after a $22 billion auction of 30-year bonds drew steady demand, providing some relief to bond markets.
The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield fell to around 5.23%, after earlier climbing to levels near its highest since 2002. However, elevated yields continued to weigh on the appeal of growth stocks, whose valuations are particularly sensitive to borrowing costs.
Investors are now looking ahead to the start of the third-quarter earnings season next week, when major U.S. banks are due to report results.

title: Meta bans TikTok ads on its platforms in US
full_text:
Nasdaq ends over 1% lower as tech stocks take a hit on OpenAI revenue report
By Rishabh Jaiswal and Mrinmay Dey
Oct 8 (Reuters) - Facebook and Instagram-owner Meta has banned advertisements by ByteDance, the Chinese parent of TikTok, on its platforms in the United States and a handful of other countries, a company spokesperson said on Thursday.
The move marks an escalation in the long-running rivalry between Meta and ByteDance, whose video-sharing app TikTok has emerged as one of Meta’s most formidable competitors for user engagement, creators and advertising dollars.
Meta’s ban takes effect immediately in the US, Canada, Egypt, Indonesia, Japan, Thailand and Vietnam, and extends to third-party advertisers running campaigns that link to TikTok and other ByteDance properties in those countries, Meta said.
"We don’t have to run ads from a competitor whose goal is to pull people off our apps," Meta said. "Declining promotional services to a competitor is a normal business practice across industries. We will continue to compete on product quality and user experience."
TikTok and ByteDance did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment on Meta’s move.
TikTok’s website shows that it does not support links that open or log users into other social media apps. However, users can still add links to their profiles that direct people to those platforms’ websites.
Meta has been urging TikTok and YouTube to follow steps it agreed to take on teen safety in August following a settlement of up to $18 billion with US states over social media harms to children.
Meta in August agreed to impose daily usage limits and restrict nighttime usage by children who use Facebook and Instagram, and enhance measures to prevent children from accessing age-restricted content.
TikTok has not publicly commented on Meta’s campaign, but it reached a settlement with Alabama in September that requires the social media platform to impose new usage limits and enhance age-verification measures for users in the state, resolving claims that it endangered children and misled consumers about its safety.
TikTok operates in the US as a majority American-owned joint venture after a deal aimed at safeguarding US user data and averting a US ban on an app used by more than 200 million users in the country.
Bloomberg News first reported Meta’s ban earlier on Thursday.

Japanese yen edges lower as household spending falls
The Japanese yen’s USD/JPY pair rose 0.1% after government data showed household spending fell for a ninth straight month in August.
Spending fell 3.1% annually, less than expectations for a 3.5% drop, and grew 0.1% month-on-month, less than estimates of 0.5%.

But the greenback was still set to add about 0.1% this week, its fourth straight week of gains.
The dollar remained close to a 1-½ year high hit earlier this week, with the minutes of the Federal Reserve’s September meeting indicating that the central bank remained hawkish. The Fed had raised rates by 25 basis points during the meeting, citing risks from inflation.
While markets priced down expectations for a hike in October, they remained confident that the Fed will raise rates by 25 bps again in December, CME Fedwatch showed.
Waning bets on an October hike saw Treasury yields fall slightly this week, although the 10-year yield remained close to its highest level since 2002.

title: Gold rises over 1% as dollar weakens, Treasury yields retreat
full_text:
Nasdaq ends over 1% lower as tech stocks take a hit on OpenAI revenue report
Investing.com-- Gold prices rose in Asian trading Friday, as a softer U.S. dollar and declining Treasury yields boosted bullion’s appeal, while investors weighed persistent inflation risks from higher oil prices.
Spot gold rose 1.1% to $4,177.83 per ounce by 22:40 ET (02:40 GMT), while U.S. Gold Futures also gained 1.1% to $4,203.40.
The dollar’s rally paused, making gold cheaper for holders of other currencies, while the benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury yield declined for a second consecutive session.
The recovery came amid a volatile backdrop for financial markets, with rising oil prices intensifying concerns that energy supply disruptions linked to the Middle East conflict could fuel inflation and prompt central banks to maintain or raise interest rates.
St. Louis Federal Reserve President Alberto Musalem said on Thursday that further monetary tightening would be needed to bring inflation back to the central bank’s 2% target within a reasonable timeframe.
He said rates could need to rise further over the next six to nine months, although he declined to indicate whether he would support an increase at the Fed’s Oct. 27-28 meeting.
Traders were pricing in an 18% probability of a rate hike in October and an 82% chance of an increase in December, according to the CME FedWatch tool. Higher interest rates tend to weigh on gold, which offers no yield, by increasing the opportunity cost of holding bullion.
Oil prices remained a key risk for bullion, with Brent crude climbing above $104 a barrel amid concerns over Middle East supply disruptions. Higher energy costs could prolong inflation pressures and reinforce expectations of tighter monetary policy, limiting gold’s upside despite its traditional role as an inflation hedge.
Meanwhile, persistent central bank demand and concerns about elevated government debt could provide support. Analysts have also pointed to expectations that China’s central bank will continue adding to its gold reserves as a potential source of demand.
Among other precious metals, silver rose 1.7% to $60.19 an ounce, while platinum gained 2.1% to $1,678.15/oz.

title: China defends yuan policy as Europe steps up pressure over trade surplus
full_text:
Nasdaq ends over 1% lower as tech stocks take a hit on OpenAI revenue report
By Yukun Zhang and Kevin Yao
BEIJING, Oct 8 (Reuters) - China pushed back against foreign criticism of its exchange-rate policy on Thursday, saying it has never pursued competitive depreciation, as European policymakers call for a stronger yuan to help curb China’s record trade surplus and export surge.
As China’s trade surplus swells, European leaders have intensified calls for a stronger yuan, fearing a "China Shock 2.0" from a fresh wave of Chinese exports.
In a lengthy policy statement, the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) rejected claims that China keeps the yuan artificially weak to gain a trade advantage, as the EU’s trade chief Maros Sefcovic is in Beijing to discuss narrowing the bloc’s trade deficit with China.
"China neither needs nor intends to obtain a trade-competitive advantage through exchange-rate depreciation, and has never engaged in competitive currency depreciation," the central bank said.
"Attributing a decline in domestic industrial competitiveness, the weakening of fiscal and financial discipline and complex structural problems simply to the exchange rates of other nations amounts to evading and shirking one’s own responsibility for making necessary adjustments."
China posted a record trade surplus of nearly $1.2 trillion in 2025, equivalent to about 6% of GDP, with analysts expecting exports of AI-related and other advanced technology products to help keep the surplus elevated this year.
China’s trade strength stems from the global competitiveness of its industries, the central bank said, arguing that countries with large trade surpluses have historically been those with strong manufacturing sectors.
European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde in June urged global leaders to discuss undervaluation of the Chinese currency as a facet of the imbalances endangering the global economy. The bloc is concerned about its trade imbalance with China, which reached €360.6 billion ($404 billion) in 2025, according to EU data, up 15% from the previous year.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has said the yuan is undervalued by 25% to 30% and called for a dialogue with China on monetary policy.
Goldman Sachs said in August that the yuan is undervalued by at least 20% on some of its valuation models, arguing that a stronger currency would help narrow China’s outsized trade and current-account surpluses and ease protectionist pressure from trading partners.
The PBOC said exchange rates reflect multiple economic and financial factors, rejecting claims that isolated model estimates prove the yuan is undervalued.
CHINA SAYS MARKET PLAYS DECISIVE ROLE
The yuan has climbed about 4% against the dollar this year despite a widening US-China yield gap.
The PBOC said the yuan has appreciated about 23% against the dollar since China’s 2005 exchange-rate reform, strengthening from 8.27 yuan per dollar to around 6.7 currently.
It warned that the yuan’s outlook remains uncertain, with forces for both appreciation and depreciation shaping its trajectory.
China lets the market play a decisive role in exchange-rate formation, the central bank said, adding that it does not preset exchange rate target levels or intervene in long-term exchange rate trends.
"The People’s Bank of China does not preset an exchange-rate target level, does not intervene in the long-term trend of the exchange rate, and maintains exchange-rate flexibility and two-way movement," it said.
China will report additional foreign exchange-related data to the International Monetary Fund starting from 2027, the central bank said.
The PBOC said China would pursue a domestic demand-led growth model under its 2026-2030 plan, boosting consumption, expanding effective investment and deepening high-level opening-up, while strengthening the domestic economy and helping drive a more balanced global economy.
($1 = 0.8937 euros)

title: OpenAI revenue reports; Delta Air Lines to report - what’s moving markets
full_text:
Nasdaq ends over 1% lower as tech stocks take a hit on OpenAI revenue report
Investing.com - Futures linked to the main U.S. indices inch up, as investors assess the outlook for the artificial intelligence boom following a series of media reports about revenues at ChatGPT-maker OpenAI. Delta Air Lines is due to unveil its latest quarterly earnings, as the carrier grapples with an uptick in fuel costs. A fresh survey of U.S. consumer sentiment could provide some insight into the mindset of U.S. households prior to the holiday shopping season.
1. Futures higher
U.S. stock futures ticked higher on Friday. By 03:04 ET (07:04 GMT), the Dow futures contract had risen by 33 points, or 0.1%, S&P 500 futures had advanced 25 points, or 0.3%, and Nasdaq 100 futures had jumped by 243 points, or 0.8%.
The main averages on Wall Street were mixed on Thursday. The blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average eked out a 0.1% gain, while the benchmark S&P 500 and tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell by 0.47% and 1.25%, respectively.
Mounting fears of a further escalation in violence in the Middle East drove the biggest daily rise in Brent crude futures in two weeks -- and subsequently fueled worries over a deepening selloff in global bond markets that has rattled sentiment throughout this week.
But oil prices later pulled back partially after President Donald Trump said the U.S. was engaged in "positive" talks with Iran and would not be attacking the country before the midterm elections. Earlier media reports had said the Pentagon was considering strike options before the November vote.
Meanwhile, a Financial Times report that OpenAI’s annualized revenue stood at about $50 billion at the end of September, short of the $70 billion that was previously signaled, weighed on tech stocks, in particular.
2. OpenAI expects annualized revenues to reach $70 billion by end-2026 - Bloomberg News
However, Nasdaq 100 futures were buoyed this morning by a Bloomberg News report which said OpenAI expects to reach or exceed $70 billion in annualized revenue by the end of the year.
The growth is expected to be driven chiefly by its enterprise business, Bloomberg said.
Annualized revenues are a critical metric for AI startups like OpenAI and rival Anthropic. The measures are used to gauge overall AI demand and the need for more computing infrastructure.
But a path to profitability for OpenAI remained unclear, with recent reports indicating that the company was still on track to slip to a full-year loss. OpenAI has also projected it will burn $280 billion by 2030.
The reports come as traders have been scrutinizing the sustainability of AI financing following news that a tidal wave of AI-linked debt deals are being utilized to help fund a massive spending binge on the infrastructure powering the nascent technology.
3. Delta Air Lines to report
On a relatively sparse earnings calendar, markets will be keeping tabs on returns from carrier Delta Air Lines before the opening bell.
For the third quarter, Delta is seen posting adjusted revenue of $17.66 billion and adjusted per-share income of $1.82, according to Bloomberg consensus estimates.
In July, Delta reiterated its full-year profit outlook and issued stronger-than-anticipated third-quarter guidance, underlining that it expects to maintain fare increases connected to a recent spike in fuel costs.
However, the group predicted that its fuel bill will be roughly $4 billion higher this year compared to the prior year, and flagged that volatility in energy prices is a major source of risk to its financial trajectory.
4. Michigan consumer sentiment report ahead
Elsewhere, a tracker of consumer expectations from the University of Michigan for October could offer a glimpse into the state of American shoppers at the beginning of the final quarter of 2026.
The Michigan consumer sentiment index is tipped to edge down to a reading of 47.5, falling from a four-month low of 48.1 in September.
Last month, respondents to the survey emphasized jitters over a continued climb in prices, although buying conditions for durable goods improved slightly because of "a perception that completing such purchases now would help consumers avoid higher prices in the future," noted Joanne Hsu, Surveys of Consumers Director at the University of Michigan.
Year-ahead inflation expectations in September jumped to the highest since June.
Overall, last month’s study revealed "broad agreement across the political spectrum" that the outlook for the economy has weakened since the beginning of the year.
5. Telecom stocks rise following SpaceX spectrum acquisition
U.S. mobile tower stocks rose in extended hours trading after SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) agreed to buy a nationwide block of low-band spectrum, which Bernstein said keeps alive the possibility that the satellite company builds a ground network.
American Tower, Crown Castle, and SBA Communications -- three of the country’s largest phone tower operators -- rose between 3% and 4.5% after-hours.
SpaceX will pay about $8 billion in cash for the spectrum to private equity firm Grain Management, the Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday.
The acquisition is aimed at improving SpaceX’s Starlink satellite-to-cellular service, with the new spectrum allowing its signal to pass through obstacles– which was a major hurdle for the service.
"This is the last critical piece of the spectrum puzzle needed for SpaceX to provide complete phone coverage in America," SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said.

Investing.com-- Apple Inc (NASDAQ:AAPL) has told some of its suppliers to cut production of components for its recently launched iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max models, Nikkei Asia reported on Friday, citing multiple people familiar with the matter.
The technology giant was seen turning more conservative on shipments since early September, with component orders for October being cut by 15%-20% from what was originally expected, the Nikkei reported.
The cuts came amid weaker-than-expected market demand for the new iPhone line, as soaring memory chip and component prices forced price hikes and dented consumer demand, the Nikkei report said.
But the Nikkei report said the weaker component demand could also be driven by Apple changing its launch schedule for the 18 series, with the company first launching the premium line– the 18 Pro, Pro Max, and the iPhone Duo– in September.
The company will launch the base iPhone 18 and an upgraded iPhone Air in early-2027. The base model iPhone was seen gaining increased popularity last year with the iPhone 17 line, and may bring in more sales for the company.
Still, the Nikkei report highlighted the growing headwinds faced by consumer electronics companies, as they struggle with rising component costs.
Global memory and electronics supplies were largely crimped by outsized demand from the artificial intelligence industry. Recent comments from memory chip major Micron suggested that this tightness was likely to persist well into 2027.

title: European stocks attempt bounce, but heads for weekly loss as French debt weighs
full_text:
Nasdaq ends over 1% lower as tech stocks take a hit on OpenAI revenue report
Investing.com - European equities mounted a tentative recovery on Friday, attempting to claw back ground from a sharp mid-week sell-off as fixed-income volatility took a breather, though bourses remain firmly on track for a negative weekly finish.
The pan-European Stoxx Europe 600 Index advanced 0.8% in early trading, snapping a bitter drop in the prior session that had dragged the regional benchmark to its lowest level in nearly four months.
France’s CAC 40 and London’s FTSE 100 rose 0.8% each, while Spain’s IBEX 35 gained 1%.
Despite Friday’s intraday bounce, the index remains down roughly 1% on the week, reflecting a week dominated by cross-asset risk reduction, hawkish central bank minutes, and escalating geopolitical friction in energy bourses.
French bond rout spills across continental bourses
Severe investor anxiety over Paris’s record-high debt load - projected at nearly 120% of GDP - and a daunting, highly fractured legislative path toward enacting €54 billion in proposed budget cuts triggered aggressive duration liquidation.
The resulting spike in French 10-year yields toward 25-year highs blew sovereign spreads over risk-free German Bunds past 140 basis points, creating a continent-wide contagion effect that pulled down Italian BTPs, Greek paper, and continental equity valuation multiples.
French equities underperformed, with the CAC 40 index hovering near its lowest levels since March and heading for an over 2% weekly decline -its second consecutive weekly loss.
French banking giants - including BNP Paribas, Credit Agricole, and Societe Generale - bore the brunt of the equity sell-off, as skyrocketing sovereign yields threatened to erode their domestic bond portfolio capital buffers, elevate debt-refinancing costs, and spark credit rating downgrade risks.
The broader spike in borrowing costs was further exacerbated by reports of massive U.S. technology corporate debt issuances, which competed directly with sovereign paper for global institutional capital and drove corporate credit spreads wider.
Energy shocks and hawkish central banks cap risk appetite
Intensified missile and drone attacks targeting commercial shipping and energy infrastructure across the Persian Gulf and Red Sea pushed crude oil back above $100 a barrel and sent wholesale natural gas surging past €80/MWh, reviving stagflationary concerns for European industrial margins.
Sentiment was further dampened by minutes from the Federal Reserve’s September meeting, which revealed that a majority of US policymakers still view further rate hikes as necessary before year-end, dashing hopes for near-term global monetary easing.
While Bank of France Governor Emmanuel Moulin acknowledged the nation’s economic situation was "serious," his explicit rejection of European Central Bank intervention reinforced to trading desks that international markets must continue to price in an elevated risk premium for European assets.

title: French yields pause near peak as markets fret over Paris’s record debt load
full_text:
Nasdaq ends over 1% lower as tech stocks take a hit on OpenAI revenue report
Investing.com - The violent sell-off across European fixed-income hubs showed signs of slowing on Friday, though sovereign borrowing costs across France and Southern Europe remained entrenched near multi-year highs as cross-asset desks weighed long-term fiscal stability risks against a backdrop of tight central bank liquidity.
While duration liquidation in Parisian paper took a breather compared to the sharp spikes seen earlier this week, the yield on France’s two-year and 10-year OATs held close to their highest levels since 2002, with the 10-year note consolidating around 4.897%.
At the policy-sensitive short end, the yield on two-year French bonds took a breather this week, heading for its first weekly decline in nine and on course to snap its longest streak of weekly yield gains since 2022.
The French fiscal crisis continued to spill over into non-core European sovereign debt bourses throughout the week.
Yields on benchmark 10-year Italian government bonds (BTPs) surged to their highest levels since mid-2023 earlier in the week, before settling near 4.95%, as international allocators demanded an elevated term premium to absorb peripheral risk.
The Greek 10-year government bond yield similarly hovered near its late-2023 highs, underscoring how non-core Eurozone issuers are bearing the collateral damage of Parisian sovereign risk premia.
Le Pen proposals offer only temporary respite against record debt
Sovereign paper had enjoyed a brief, temporary reprieve earlier in the week after far-right leader Marine Le Pen sought to reassure international markets by unveiling an ambitious budget plan aimed at slashing France’s public deficit to 3% of GDP by 2030 through €140 billion in net spending cuts.
However, trading desks quickly treated the announcement with skepticism, viewing the proposed fiscal consolidation as politically difficult to enforce given the deeply fractured makeup of the French National Assembly ahead of the 2027 presidential election.
With France’s debt-to-GDP ratio hovering near a record 120% and its 2026 budget deficit projected at 5.4% - far exceeding the EU’s 3% ceiling - investors have continued to demand a wide spread over risk-free German Bunds.
The structural pressure was further compounded by Bank of France Governor Emmanuel Moulin, who explicitly noted that while the nation’s economic situation was "serious," Paris did not require backstops from the European Central Bank.
Safe-haven core anchors German bunds
Germany’s 10-year government bond yield - the benchmark for the single-currency bloc - held steady around 3.498%, remaining well below its peripheral peers as safe-haven bids capped yield increases.
The two-year German Bund yield consolidated near 3.055%. The downward drift reflects growing money market consensus that the ECB will maintain a cautious, data-dependent policy stance as elevated sovereign yields and high energy prices tighten financial conditions across the bloc.

title: OpenAI says it has fired three researchers for violating sensitive information policy
full_text:
Nasdaq ends over 1% lower as tech stocks take a hit on OpenAI revenue report
Oct 9 (Reuters) - OpenAI fired three of its researchers last week after an investigation found they violated policies on handling sensitive information, the AI major said in a post on X on Friday.
OpenAI’s statement comes after the dismissed researchers Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni published a letter outlining the circumstances of their termination, arguing that their abrupt firing could create uncertainty among remaining employees and undermine the culture that previously allowed researchers to raise safety concerns.
"I believe we were fired for prioritizing safety over the near-term interests of OpenAI as a corporation," Balesni said in an X post that accompanied the letter.
OpenAI, however, asserted that the dismissal was not related to raising safety concerns or speaking out.
"Our internal investigation uncovered a significant breach of trust beyond what’s outlined in the letter they published and we stand by the decision to not continue their employment," OpenAI said.
"Safety and research debates happen every day at OpenAI, often spirited and highly critical. We actively encourage these discussions and consider them essential to making the right decisions...We have not and do not terminate any of our employees for raising concerns," it said.
While OpenAI did not reveal the specifics of the alleged violations, Wang, Korbak, and Balesni said in their letter that they were not the source of a news article published on The Information last month about security concerns around OpenAI’s latest AI model ’Astra’.
This comes as current and former researchers at major AI firms OpenAI, Google DeepMind, and Anthropic warn that companies are doing too little to guard against the potential fallout of building self-improving AI systems that could become difficult for humans to control.
In July, OpenAI agents broke out of their testing arena and hacked AI firm Hugging Face.

title: EU telecom stocks fall after SpaceX’s move to become a wireless carrier
full_text:
Nasdaq ends over 1% lower as tech stocks take a hit on OpenAI revenue report
Investing.com -- European telecom stocks fell Friday after Space Exploration Technologies said it will buy a nationwide U.S. spectrum portfolio, a push to turn Starlink into a full-fledged mobile carrier.
Deutsche Telekom slumped 7% in European trading by 07:27 GMT, Vodafone shed 3.1%, and Orange SA fell 2.6%. Telefonica slid 2.5%, and BT Group slipped 1.4%, while Koninklijke lost 2.1%.
Shares of U.S. telecom giants AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile also dropped in extended trading Thursday after The Wall Street Journal first reported the deal.
SpaceX agreed to buy the portfolio from Grain Management, a digital infrastructure investor, in a deal subject to Federal Communications Commission (FCC) approval. It covers up to 14 megahertz of paired spectrum in the 800 MHz band.
"This prime low-band spectrum addresses one of the key remaining technical gaps that will pave the way for Starlink Mobile to become a major mobile carrier in the U.S.," SpaceX said. CEO Elon Musk called it a "very big deal" in a post on X.
Unlike satellite spectrum, the licenses are suited to service from cellphone towers. Once the FCC approves, SpaceX said it will pair its growing satellite constellation with "an advanced terrestrial deployment," covering places satellites can’t reach, including inside buildings. The FCC earlier this week approved SpaceX’s bid to launch up to 15,000 satellites dedicated to mobile service.
SpaceX appears intent on competing with the carriers directly. Last week, T-Mobile, AT&T and Verizon formed a joint venture to expand satellite coverage in underserved areas, without Starlink. T-Mobile has also removed mentions of Starlink from its T-Satellite promotions.
SpaceX has offered basic wireless connections in remote areas through a T-Mobile partnership for more than a year and has been upgrading its network with newer satellites that carry more data. Last year it agreed to a roughly $17 billion cash-and-stock deal for satellite spectrum rights from EchoStar, later adding $2.6 billion of EchoStar’s ground-based licenses.

title: OMV shares fall as weaker chemicals, Mideast liftings weigh on Q3
full_text:
Nasdaq ends over 1% lower as tech stocks take a hit on OpenAI revenue report
Investing.com -- Shares in Austria’s OMV fell 2% on Friday after the oil and gas group said a weaker chemicals business and a shortfall in Middle East crude liftings would weigh on third-quarter earnings, offsetting a surge in refining margins.
The clean operating result of OMV’s chemicals business is expected to be “materially lower” than in the second quarter, mainly because of a “substantially weaker” market for Borouge International in all regions, the company said.
European polyethylene prices averaged €2,263 a tonne in the third quarter, against €2,655 in the second, and the European ethylene margin was €675 a tonne, against €813.
In energy, OMV expects a headwind of about €100 million to the clean operating result because no crude liftings took place in the Middle East and lifting schedules in other countries cut sales volumes, it said.
That increased an underlift position, which OMV expects to recover through future liftings. Total hydrocarbon sales volumes were 225 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day, against 242 in the second quarter.
Refining was the offset. Income from ADNOC Refining and ADNOC Global Trading is expected to rise substantially from the second quarter, mainly because of higher refinery use in a strong refining margin environment.
OMV’s European refining margin indicator, based on Brent, averaged $37.50 a barrel, against $20.33 in the second quarter. OMV said retail and commercial margins are expected to be significantly lower than in the second quarter. It gave no reason.
At group level, solidarity contributions in Austria and Romania are expected to have a negative impact of between €150 million and €200 million on reported net income. OMV said they are recorded as special items, so they do not affect clean operating result or clean net income.
OMV received dividends of about €460 million from Borouge International in the quarter. It expects cash outflows of about €200 million for certificates under Germany’s Fuel Emissions Trading Act, which it typically bought in the fourth quarter in previous years.

Oct 9 (Reuters) - Major European companies are expected to report substantially higher third-quarter earnings, the latest LSEG I/B/E/S data showed on Thursday, although the year-on-year growth should slightly temper from the previous quarter.
Companies on Europe’s benchmark STOXX 600 index are expected to report quarterly earnings growth of 21% on aggregate, mostly buoyed by the energy and basic materials sectors.
That is an improvement compared to last week’s forecast for 19.4% growth and would mark the second-best quarterly profit growth in the past 14 quarters. Excluding the energy sector, the expected growth rate for STOXX 600 companies is a more modest 9.7%.
European blue-chip companies’ revenues are seen increasing by 10.6% from a year ago, also above the average of the past couple of years.
"Demand is strong enough to allow companies to pass on higher prices which leads to higher sales. At the same time, energy costs make up a smaller share of sales than headlines would suggest," a Deutsche Bank report said earlier this week.
European energy majors have been benefiting from the consequences of the US-Israeli war with Iran and from Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian refineries, which have sharply cut exports from some of the world’s biggest producers of fossil fuels.
They are now expected to post profit growth of 115.9% for the third quarter, according to the LSEG report.
Meanwhile, companies in the European real estate sector are seen delivering earnings 71.5% smaller than in the same period last year.
Next week, investors will be closely looking at results of chip equipment supplier ASML, Europe’s most valuable listed company, and Swedish telecoms equipment maker Ericsson to assess the tone of the earnings season.
